newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares fall on trade data, ahead of FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares fall on trade data, ahead of FOMC.

text.p: Singapore's key share index closed lower on Monday as blue chips fell on Friday's poor Singapore export figures and on a lack of institutional buyers.

"Most of the institutional buyers are waiting to see if U.S. interest rates will change at the FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) meeting later this evening," said an insititutional dealer with a foreign brokerage.
By the 0900 GMT close, the benchmark Straits Times Industrials index (STII) was down 31.07 points at 2,156.79.
STII stocks Fraser & Neave and Cycle & Carriage were down 60 cents and 40 cents at Singapore $14.60 and S$15.10 respectively.
"There is some interest in bank stocks but at a lower price. There are definitely more sellers than buyers," said the dealer.
Most dealers said the index would trade sideways or fall on Tuesday depending on the outcome of the FOMC meeting.

The most active stock was electronics company Goldtron with 18.92 million shares changing hands on speculation Mokhzani Mahathir, son of the Malaysian prime minister, was accumulating its shares. Goldtron's share rose half a cent S$0.91.
Friday's trade data showed a 6.3 percent year-on-year drop in Singapore non-oil exports in August thanks mainly to a fall in electronics sales.
